name: Shehab Elorabi
title: General Manager
biography: Shehab Elorabi, currently General Manager of Modon International Real Estate, Egypt, comes with a wealth of experience in the real estate development field, with vast exposure to both local and international real estate markets. Shehab has worked in Dubai for both Nakheel and Dubai Properties. He has also served as Managing Director at Hassan Allam Properties from 2022 to 2024, after having served as Sodic’s Chief Operating Officer from 2018 to 2022. His earlier career which started in the USA, focused on construction and project management of mega-scale projects including Power Plants, Hotels, Hospitality projects, as well as Commercial and Residential Real Estate Developments. He has a diverse and unique technical and business management experience that extends over 35 years.

name: Tamer Sakr
title: Founder and COO
biography: With more than 22 years of experience in digital transformation and business development, Tamer Sakr is the Founder & COO of DiTa BC, a consultancy and digital transformation firm operating across Egypt and the USA, helping SMEs and startups turn ambition into measurable results. For more than eight years, he worked at the EBRD (European Bank for Reconstruction and Development), where he led and managed non-financial advisory projects for hundreds of enterprises. His earlier career spans business development, international trade promotion, and IT management, including market-entry initiatives for Dubai Exports across Saudi Arabia and Egypt. He holds an MBA with distinction from the Arab Academy. Today, he works side by side with founders and leadership teams to unlock growth, resolve operational bottlenecks, and implement digital solutions that let organizations scale with confidence.

name: Ziad AbdelTawab
title: Supreme Council of Culture member
biography: Assistant Secretary-General for Information Systems and Digital Transformation at the Cabinet of Ministers, Arab Republic of Egypt (since September 2019). He has been a member of the Supreme Council of Culture since July 2025. He serves as Rapporteur of the Digital Culture and Cultural Information Infrastructure Committee at the Supreme Council of Culture (since March 2020) and has been a member of the same committee since November 2023. He is the First Deputy Chairman of the Egyptian Esports Federation (2022), a member of the Advisory Board for the "Digital Egypt" initiative (2022), and a member of the Advisory Body for the Youth Research Program at the National Center for Social and Criminological Research (since 2024). He also wrote a daily column for *Rose al-Yusuf* newspaper from 2018 to 2024. He held several positions at the Cabinet’s Information and Decision Support Center (IDSC), including: Head of the IDSC and Head of the National Committee for Crises and Disasters (2018–2019); Director of the Communications and Networks Department and Deputy Head of the Information Technology and Projects Sector (2011–2018); and Communications and Networks Engineer (1995–2001). Additionally, he was a member of the Supreme Council for Cybersecurity (2014–2020) and a member of the technical team that contributed to localizing the Internet within Egyptian government entities during the 1990s. He authors numerous specialized articles for various magazines—such as *Al-Siyassa Al-Dawliya* (International Politics), *Al-Democratiya* (Democracy), *Al-Hilal*, *Al-Musawwar*, *Al-Ahram Al-Iqtisadi*, and *Lughat Al-Asr*—as well as for websites including *Al-Siyassa Al-Dawliya*, *Al-Ahram Al-Masa'i*, *Kalimatuna*, *Arabian Utopia*, and *Nabta* magazine. He possesses over 30 years of experience in consulting, designing, and managing information systems, telecommunications networks, digital transformation solutions, information security, and artificial intelligence. His expertise extends to designing and managing systems for crisis and disaster management and government complaint handling, as well as developing information centers and conducting studies on decision support and development. He has served on examination committees for numerous Master’s and PhD theses in fields such as information technology, economics, political science, media studies, and specialized education. He has participated in various judging panels for information and communication technology (ICT) projects and cultural competitions. He has published eight books on digital transformation and the information age: 1. *Zero One: An Introduction to Digital Awareness* (2021) 2. *Artificial Intelligence and Data Analysis* (2022) 3. *A Guide to the Ethics of Using AI Applications in Scientific Research* (2022) 4. *The Gang... Putting ChatGPT on Trial* (2025) 5. *Bahia... The Future of Digital Culture in Egypt* (2025) 6. *Generation Alpha Innovates for Egypt* (2025) – Supreme Council of Culture / National Center for Child Culture / State Award for the Young Creator 7. *Reflections on the Information Age... Technology and AI: Where Are We and Where Are We Headed?* (2025) 2026 Supreme Council of Culture The eighth edition, titled "Culture 2.0: Artificial Intelligence and Reshaping," 2026. He holds a Master’s degree in Information Technology and Business Administration (2000) from Middlesex University in the United Kingdom and a Bachelor’s degree in Telecommunications and Electronics Engineering (1994) from Cairo University. He has been honored by numerous institutions and bodies; notably, he was recognized by the Egyptian Ministry of Culture as one of the "Makers of Egyptian Identity" during the inaugural "Culture Day" in January 2025. Most recently, he received the Arab Media Excellence Award in Digital Media from the League of Arab States—in recognition of his role in raising awareness about digital media—on the sidelines of the 55th session of the Council of Arab Information Ministers, held at the League’s General Secretariat headquarters in Cairo in October 2025.

name: Nada Akrab
title: Senior Business Development Manager
biography: Senior Business Development Manager at Vezeeta, Egypt's largest digital health platform, driving growth in Health Tech through channel partnerships and business development. I lead Pharma Partnerships across Egypt and KSA, building and scaling strategic relationships with leading pharmaceutical companies. I also own Education as a standalone BD channel — covering universities, schools, nurseries, academies, and e-learning platforms — and I'm driving the expansion of Shamel, our healthcare subscription e-card product.

name: Ahmed Eissa
title: CEO
biography: EG-Insurtech harnesses advanced AI intelligence to accelerate insight, enhance decision-making, and unify all stakeholders through smarter, connected systems. As the creators of Egypt’s first full-fledged flagship insurance core system, we continue to redefine innovation and set new standards for the industry.

name: Amr Soliman
title: co-founder & chairman
biography: A veteran in the financial technology space, leading a software solutions company since 1999. “eVision” designs & builds specialized technology solutions for the banking & finance industry in Egypt and the MEA Region. Eng Soliman is also a co-founder and chairman of Tarmiiz.com, a startup in the field of Real World Asset Tokenization based on blockchain technology. With a bachelor degree in construction engineering and a masters of science in Project Management for National Development Projects, Eng. Soliman kicked off his career spending 5 years working for the Egypt Social Fund for Development, with diverse experiences from managing public works and community development projects, to micro & sme loans programs, to donor management and financial control of funds. This has very much shaped Eng. Soliman’s deep belief in sustainable development. Eng. Soliman chairs the Economic & Environment committees at the National Council for Women (NCW) since 2016, and spearheads the National financial inclusion program for digital village group saving and lending for the rural women of Egypt. “Ta7wisha” is a technology platform designed to organize the women in groups, link financial institutions, avail digital saving, instant micro loans and micro investment opportunities; and accumulate individual/group credit history. Data is leveraged to attract green finance for rural women led, environment friendly, sustainable revenue generating projects. Eng. Soliman also sits on the boards of Nasser Social Bank, the Rural & Environmental Industries Support Fund, and the National Steering Committee for Women Financial Inclusion with the Central Bank of Egypt and the Federation of Micro Finance.

name: Seif El Kilany
title: Co-founder & CEO
biography: Seif El Kilany is Co-Founder and CEO of Tarmiiz, which builds tokenization infrastructure for issuers and asset managers, and for the regulators that supervise them. Before founding Tarmiiz, Seif spent over 18 years building and operating electronic trading and market infrastructure for US equities and ETFs. He holds a Master's in Finance from Boston University and a BSc in Computer Science from Concordia University, with a blockchain strategy specialization from INSEAD.

name: Mahmoud Gebril
title: Assistant Chairman
biography: Mahmoud Gebril joined Beltone Markets Division- one of the fastest growing financial institutions in the MENA region – in March 2024 as Managing Director & Head of Product Development in the markets division. With over 25 years of experience in treasury management, asset management, in the financial services industry in Egypt, he drives the company’s strategic growth and development. Gebril was previously the Head of corporate finance at Financial Regulatory Authority (2019-2023). Prior to that, he began his career in the banking sector with Misr Iran Development bank in field of capital market and dealing room (1997-2006), Gebril joined National Fund Management Company (2006-2007), responsible for fixed income and equity capital markets and asset management, he was appointed executive manager, he has equipped as Managing Director of AMWAL financial investments (2007-2019). He holds a Bachelor of Commerce from Cairo University, A Capital Markets analysis postgraduate diploma from Faculty of Economics & Political Science – Cairo University and A Fundamentals of Islamic Finance Diploma from “IFF” London.

name: Reham ElMorally
title: Head of Public Policy and Research
biography: Dr. Reham ElMorally is a policy strategist, academic, and author whose work connects innovation, entrepreneurship, and inclusive economic development. She is Head of Public Policy and Research at Entlaq Holdings, Assistant Professor in Global Affairs and Public Policy at the American University in Cairo, and Gender Studies Collection Editor at Lived Places Publishing. At Entlaq, she has directed more than 22 research and advisory projects, including national entrepreneurship diagnostics and initiatives with UNDP, UNIDO, and GIZ. Drawing on research across five countries, she translates complex evidence into practical policy recommendations and investment insights for governments, development partners, and businesses. Her expertise spans startup ecosystems, climate technology, digital agriculture, and women’s entrepreneurship, with a focus on removing barriers that prevent innovation from delivering economic and social impact. Across her work in policy, academia, and publishing, Dr. ElMorally follows a guiding philosophy: “looking for the silences”; asking whose experiences are missing from the evidence, whose perspectives are absent from the classroom, and whose stories remain unpublished. Inspired by Simone de Beauvoir, she approaches self-knowledge and the pursuit of understanding as acts of courage that demand questioning inherited assumptions. Whether advising institutions, teaching future leaders, or championing authors, she brings overlooked perspectives into the conversations that shape knowledge, opportunity, and change.

name: Mathias Dittrich
title: Senior Manager – Investment Management
biography: Leading investment efforts of SANAD Fund for MSME. Always on the lookout for new potential investees!

name: Germine Bouchnack
title: Executive Director
biography: Germine Bouchnack is an Executive Director at Middle East Venture Partners (MEVP), with over nine years of experience across venture capital, banking, and the entrepreneurship ecosystem. Prior to joining MEVP, Germine was part of the investment team at Flat6Labs, where she helped manage a portfolio of more than 55 startups across diverse sectors. She previously worked at Commercial International Bank (CIB), where she collaborated with senior management on the strategic transformation of the bank’s SME Banking business, including its strategy, products, and processes. Germine holds a bachelor’s degree in Management Technology, with a double major in Economics and Finance, from the German University in Cairo. Her engagement with entrepreneurship began during her undergraduate years, when she led several entrepreneurial initiatives and conducted her bachelor’s thesis on Egypt’s SME financing landscape.

name: Omar Ellaithy
title: Managing Partner & Co Founder
biography: Omar Ellaithy is an entrepreneur and business leader with a background in banking and a passion for building businesses that create meaningful impact. Today, Omar is the Co-Founder & Managing Partner of Babyfit Academy, an infant swimming academy focused on introducing children to sports and building the foundation for a healthy, active lifestyle from as early as two months old. Omar began his professional journey in banking at CIB (Commercial International Bank) before transitioning into entrepreneurship and pursuing his passion for building and developing businesses. A graduate of Cairo University’s Faculty of Commerce, English Section, Omar’s journey reflects his belief in turning ideas into meaningful experiences and businesses that create real value for people and communities.

name: Menna Abdelhady
title: Project Manager
biography: I’m a Biotechnologist passionate about Business especially where Science and Business come together. I’m currently a Master’s Student at the Faculty of Science Cairo University, while working as a Senior Account Manager at Nawah Scientific. My role allows me to combine my scientific background with business development, account management, and building strong relationships with researchers, universities, students, and organizations. Through my experience in Biotechnology and Life Sciences I’ve developed a strong interest in understanding scientific needs and turning them into business opportunities, partnerships, and practical solutions. Alongside my work in Life Sciences, I’ve been working in Event Management for the past four years, managing and supporting different conferences, events, and initiatives with nearly 5,000 attendees in total. This experience has allowed me to develop strong skills in event management, communication, partnerships, and community engagement. What connects everything I do is my passion for Science, Business, and people. I believe a scientific background can open opportunities beyond the lab especially when combined with business, communication, entrepreneurship, and strong connections between people and industries.

name: Amany Helmy
title: Founder & CEO
biography: Amany Helmy is a seasoned HR entrepreneur, founder, and people strategist with a strong track record across Egypt and the Middle East. As the Founder & CEO of Blissify, she helps businesses build stronger cultures, smarter people systems, and higher-performing teams through innovative HR consulting, employee engagement, and practical learning experiences. With deep expertise in talent, performance, and organizational development, Amany is known for blending strategic HR with human-centered impact.

name: Amr Saleh
title: Head of AI Transformation
biography: Amr leads AI Transformation at Bosta, Egypt's leading last-mile delivery and logistics platform. He's also chairman and investor at Taalam.ai, empowering Arabs to learn AI tools for the professional workspace, and a serial entrepreneur: former CEO of Miran (AI-powered health and fitness app in Saudi Arabia), co-founder of Elk (blockchain tools for makers), and co-founder of Integreight, the company behind 1Sheeld, which raised 8.5x its Kickstarter goal and shipped to 50+ countries.

name: Dalia Elbadry
title: Business Growth Manager
biography: Dalia El Badry is a leading expert in Social Entrepreneurship and project management, particularly in the realm of incubation and acceleration programs that support female empowerment. With a Master's in Marketing and a Marketing Diplomat from Alexandria University, Dalia has extensive experience in the tech industry. Dalia's hands-on approach and deep understanding of incubator operations have earned her recognition as a top performer in TOT programs related to management and incubation. She has honed her skills as a trainer and consultant through her participation in these programs, and her experience has made her a sought-after resource for startups and entrepreneurs. Her expertise in management and incubation has been honed through years of hands-on experience and training, making her a valuable asset to any organization looking to grow and succeed.

name: Ahmed Wadi
title: Founder and CEO
biography: Ahmed Wadi: Founder & CEO, Money Fellows My professional journey has always been defined by a singular focus: identifying fundamental human needs and building the technology to meet them. This path began with my first venture, Objectly, a startup dedicated to developing item-tracking software. It was a pivotal learning experience, resulting in technology that was subsequently adopted by industry giants like Microsoft and Daimler. While my academic background—a B.Sc. in Computer Science from the University of Stuttgart (2009) and an M.Sc. in IT from the Technical University of Munich (2014)—equipped me with the technical tools, the inspiration for Money Fellows was born from personal necessity. During my time in Germany, I sought personal financing only to discover that the available options required an extensive credit history—a barrier that excluded thousands of otherwise eligible individuals. I was immediately reminded of the traditional Egyptian "Gameya" (ROSCA), a model of communal saving and financing I had watched my family rely on since childhood. I saw how effective these money circles were for millions in Egypt and across the region, yet they lacked convenience. They were limited by personal networks, availability of slots, and the friction of physical payments and collection. I realized that by applying modern fintech infrastructure, we could solve the issues of scalability and security while preserving the community spirit of the model. Today, Money Fellows is not just a fintech company; we are a bridge connecting tradition with technology, delivering essential, secure, and inclusive financial services to our community.
